dubbiññeyyo.meaning_2: hard to understand; difficult to know; hard to comprehend
dubbiññeyyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text. The du- prefix assimilates to the following v-; viññeyya is a potential participle of vijānāti.
dubbiññeyyo.example_1: Yo hi so sikkhāpadapaññattisamayo sāriputtādīhipi dubbiññeyyo, tena samayena hetubhūtena karaṇabhūtena ca sikkhāpadāni paññāpayanto sikkhāpadapaññattihetuñca apekkhamāno bhagavā tattha tattha vihāsi, tasmā tadatthajotanatthaṃ tattha karaṇavacanena niddeso kato.
dubbiññeyyo.translation_1: Because the Blessed One resided here and there waiting for the 'occasion' (samaya) of the laying down of the training rule—which was difficult for even the Elder Sāriputta and others to know—and because he dwelt there while anticipating the cause for that laying down of the training rule, the instrumental case was used there to indicate that meaning.

riyāpathesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text; stands for iriyāpatha with the initial i elided after a preceding vowel or in compound.
riyāpathesu.translation_1: However, here it is a designation of the yoga of one of the postures—standing, walking, sitting, or lying down.

vanute.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The commentary explains vana ('wood') as from vanute ('begs'), but the verb is actually √van + o. 3rd singular present middle. The form is vanute.
vanute.example_1: Vanute iti vā vanaṃ , nānāvidhakusuma-gandhasammodamattakokilādivihaṅgamābhirutehi mandamālutacalitarukkhasākhāviṭapapallavapalāsehi ca ‘‘ etha maṃ paribhuñjathā ’’ ti sabbapāṇino yācati viyāti attho.
vanute.translation_1: Or it is called ‘wood’ (vana) because it begs, as if it were pleading with all beings, saying, ‘Come, enjoy me,’ with the beautiful sounds of various birds like cuckoos intoxicated by the fragrance of flowers, and with the branches, twigs, and leaves of trees trembling in the gentle breeze.

tadatthaparinipphādanaṃ.meaning_2: accomplishment of that purpose; fulfilment of that aim; attainment of that benefit
tadatthaparinipphādanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of tad + attha + parinipphādana (pari + ni + √pad, caus). Nominative singular in the text, parallel with tadanurūpavihāraṃ; alternatively the doer of the purpose, i.e. the one who accomplishes that aim, may be implied.
tadatthaparinipphādanaṃ.example_1: Katamo ekapuggalo, tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho ’’ ti (a. ni.1.170) vacanato yadatthaṃ bhagavā uppanno, tadatthaparinipphādanaṃ, pacchimena yattha uppanno, tadanurūpavihāraṃ.
tadatthaparinipphādanaṃ.translation_1: By the latter, he shows his dwelling appropriate to the place where he was born.

suvaṇṇavalayānūpurādisaṅghaṭṭanasaddasam.meaning_2: inhabited by household people whose sweet voices, mingled with the sound of golden bracelets, anklets and so on clashing, speak and laugh; where the people of the house move about, their sweet voices mixed with the sound of gold bangles and anklets striking together, talking and laughing
suvaṇṇavalayānūpurādisaṅghaṭṭanasaddasam.construction: suvaṇṇa + valaya + anūpura + ādi + saṅghaṭṭana + sadda + sammissita + kathita + hasita + madhura + sara + gehajana + vicarita
suvaṇṇavalayānūpurādisaṅghaṭṭanasaddasam.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular qualifying mahāgharassa. Very long bahubbīhi compound; the boundary gehajana (< geha + jana) and the reading viharita for vicarita are both possible.
suvaṇṇavalayānūpurādisaṅghaṭṭanasaddasam.example_1: Ettāvatā ca yaṃ āyasmatā ānandena kamalakuvalayujjalavimalasādurasasalilāya pokkharaṇiyā sukhāvataraṇatthaṃ nimmalasilātalaracanavilāsasobhitaratanasopānaṃ vippakiṇṇamuttātalasadisavālikākiṇṇapaṇḍarabhūmibhāgaṃ titthaṃ viya suvibhattabhittivicitravedikāparikkhittassa nakkhattapathaṃ phusitukāmatāya viya, vijambhitasamussayassa pāsādavarassa sukhārohaṇatthaṃ dantamaya-saṇhamuduphalaka-kañcanalatāvinaddha- maṇigaṇappabhāsamudayujjalasobhaṃ sopānaṃ viya, suvaṇṇavalayānūpurādisaṅghaṭṭanasaddasammissitakathitahasitamadhurassaragehajanavicaritassa uḷāraissariyavibhavasobhitassa mahāgharassa sukhappavesanatthaṃ suvaṇṇarajatamaṇimuttāpavāḷādijutivissaravijjotita-suppatiṭṭhitavisāladvārabāhaṃ mahādvāraṃ viya ca atthabyañjanasampannassa buddhānaṃ desanāñāṇagambhīrabhāvasaṃsūcakassa imassa suttassa sukhāvagāhaṇatthaṃ kāladesadesakavatthuparisāpadesapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ nidānaṃ bhāsitaṃ, tassa atthavaṇṇanā samattā.
suvaṇṇavalayānūpurādisaṅghaṭṭanasaddasam.translation_1: With this, the commentary on the meaning of the introduction—which was spoken to ensure easy access to this sutta, which is endowed with meaning and phrasing and indicative of the depth of the Buddhas’ teaching knowledge, and which is adorned with the time, place, teacher, and assembly—has been completed, much like a grand palace that is adorned with steps made of jewels, with floors of white sand like scattered pearl dust, and with vast, well-secured doors shining with the light of gold, silver, jewels, pearls, and coral, built to allow easy entry into a great house adorned by the splendor of great wealth, and built like a stairway of polished ivory, golden vines, and the light of jewel clusters, to allow easy ascent into a lofty palace adorned with the sounds of gold bangles and anklets, and the sweet voices of people living there, and much like a clear pool of water possessing sweet, cool, and stainless water, with steps made of beautiful stones that are adorned with fine stairs to allow easy descent.

sukhāvagāhaṇatthaṃ.meaning_2: easy to enter; easy to penetrate; easily comprehended
sukhāvagāhaṇatthaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Attributive to nidāna; the reading sukhāvatarana in the preceding sentence suggests the two words alternate in the commentary. In the text it is used in the accusative singular as part of the compound sukhāvagāhaṇatthaṃ.
sukhāvagāhaṇatthaṃ.example_1: Ettāvatā ca yaṃ āyasmatā ānandena kamalakuvalayujjalavimalasādurasasalilāya pokkharaṇiyā sukhāvataraṇatthaṃ nimmalasilātalaracanavilāsasobhitaratanasopānaṃ vippakiṇṇamuttātalasadisavālikākiṇṇapaṇḍarabhūmibhāgaṃ titthaṃ viya suvibhattabhittivicitravedikāparikkhittassa nakkhattapathaṃ phusitukāmatāya viya, vijambhitasamussayassa pāsādavarassa sukhārohaṇatthaṃ dantamaya-saṇhamuduphalaka-kañcanalatāvinaddha- maṇigaṇappabhāsamudayujjalasobhaṃ sopānaṃ viya, suvaṇṇavalayānūpurādisaṅghaṭṭanasaddasammissitakathitahasitamadhurassaragehajanavicaritassa uḷāraissariyavibhavasobhitassa mahāgharassa sukhappavesanatthaṃ suvaṇṇarajatamaṇimuttāpavāḷādijutivissaravijjotita-suppatiṭṭhitavisāladvārabāhaṃ mahādvāraṃ viya ca atthabyañjanasampannassa buddhānaṃ desanāñāṇagambhīrabhāvasaṃsūcakassa imassa suttassa sukhāvagāhaṇatthaṃ kāladesadesakavatthuparisāpadesapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ nidānaṃ bhāsitaṃ, tassa atthavaṇṇanā samattā.
sukhāvagāhaṇatthaṃ.translation_1: With this, the commentary on the meaning of the introduction—which was spoken to ensure easy access to this sutta, which is endowed with meaning and phrasing and indicative of the depth of the Buddhas’ teaching knowledge, and which is adorned with the time, place, teacher, and assembly—has been completed, much like a grand palace that is adorned with steps made of jewels, with floors of white sand like scattered pearl dust, and with vast, well-secured doors shining with the light of gold, silver, jewels, pearls, and coral, built to allow easy entry into a great house adorned by the splendor of great wealth, and built like a stairway of polished ivory, golden vines, and the light of jewel clusters, to allow easy ascent into a lofty palace adorned with the sounds of gold bangles and anklets, and the sweet voices of people living there, and much like a clear pool of water possessing sweet, cool, and stainless water, with steps made of beautiful stones that are adorned with fine stairs to allow easy descent.

votiādinā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] No sentences were supplied, and the form votiādinā is not clearly attested in the related entries. It may be a compound ending in -ādi used instrumentally, but the reading is uncertain and needs checking against the commentary context.

paridayhantīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural present in -nti, quoted with -ti (paridayhantīti = paridayhanti + iti).
paridayhantīti.example_1: Yathāha – puthu kilese janentīti puthujjanā, puthu avihatasakkāyadiṭṭhikāti puthujjanā, puthu satthārānaṃ mukhamullokikāti puthujjanā, puthu sabbagatīhi avuṭṭhitāti puthujjanā, puthu nānābhisaṅkhāre abhisaṅkharontīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāoghehi vuyhantīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāsantāpehi santappantīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāpariḷāhehi paridayhantīti puthujjanā, puthu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu rattā giddhā gadhitā mucchitā ajjhosannā laggā lagitā palibuddhāti puthujjanā, puthu pañcahi nīvaraṇehi āvuṭā nivutā ovutā pihitā paṭicchannā paṭikujjitāti puthujjanāti (mahāni.51).
paridayhantīti.translation_1: As it is said: ‘They are called ordinary persons because they give rise to many defilements; they are ordinary persons because they have not destroyed the many [types of] personality view; they are ordinary persons because they look up to many [different] teachers; they are ordinary persons because they have not risen from the many [types of] states of existence; they are ordinary persons because they accumulate many [varied] formations; they are ordinary persons because they are swept away by many [varied] floods; they are ordinary persons because they burn with many [varied] torments; they are ordinary persons because they scorch with many [varied] burning sensations; they are ordinary persons because they are infatuated, greedy, tied, infatuated, clinging, caught, entangled, and obstructed in the many five strands of sensuality; they are ordinary persons because they are covered, hidden, swaddled, shut off, concealed, and upside-down in the many five hindrances.’

putiso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text has putiso, probably a misreading or variant of puriso (nominative singular of purisa, 'person; man'); note the commentary glosses puggaladesanā just after. Treat as doubtful; if purisa is intended, lemma_1 purisa, lemma_2 puriso, pos masc, pattern a masc, stem puris.
putiso.example_1: ‘‘ Cha dhātuyo ayaṃ putiso cha phassāyatano aṭṭhārasa manopavicāro caturādhiṭṭhāno ’’ ti (ma. ni.3.343) evarūpī dhammādhiṭṭhānā puggaladesanā.
putiso.translation_1: ‘This person has six elements, six sense-spheres, eighteen mental movements, four foundations’ — such is a Dhamma-based personal-teaching.

ayalohādīsu.meaning_2: iron and copper; iron and metal
ayalohādīsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of aya (iron) and loha (copper, metal). In the text it is part of a bahubbīhi compound ayalohādīsu (ayaloha-ādīsu), locative plural, meaning 'in iron, copper, and the like'. The commentary explains that people develop desire for such metals.
ayalohādīsu.translation_1: Indeed, they generate a craving desire for iron, metals, and so on.

ayalohādīni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound with ādi used adverbially to mean 'iron and the rest'; nominative plural neuter in the text.
ayalohādīni.example_1: Ayalohādīni assādeti abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
ayalohādīni.translation_1: They relish, delight in, and remain holding to iron, metals, and so on.

ayādīni.meaning_2: iron and the rest; iron etc.
ayādīni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text ayādīni is accusative plural, matching the external earth (pathaviṃ); aya here means iron, not the pronoun ayaṃ.
ayādīni.example_1: Mama ayo mama lohantiādinā nayena ayādīni mamāyati rakkhati gopayati, evaṃ bāhiraṃ pathaviṃ taṇhāmaññanāya maññati.
ayādīni.translation_1: By way of such methods as ‘My iron, my metal,’ they cherish, guard, and protect iron, etc.; thus, they conceive the external earth through craving-conceiving.

ayalohādayo.meaning_2: iron and metals; iron, copper, and the like
ayalohādayo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text ayalohādayo is separated in the commentary as ayaloha + ādayo ('iron and metals, etc.'); ayalohādiupakaraṇo in the same sentence supports this analysis. Nominative plural. Doubtful whether the sandhi is ayalohā + ādayo or ayaloha + ādayo; the reading ayalohādiupakaraṇo suggests ayalohādi + upakaraṇa.
ayalohādayo.example_1: Iti me ayalohādayo siyuṃ anāgatamaddhānanti vā panettha nandiṃ samannāneti, imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā evaṃ sampannaayalohādiupakaraṇo bhavissāmī ’’ ti appaṭiladdhassa paṭilābhāya cittaṃ paṇidahati.
ayalohādayo.translation_1: ‘May my iron and metals be like this in the future,’ or setting their mind on obtaining what they have not yet obtained by way of such methods as, ‘By this virtue or by this holy life, I will be one who possesses complete equipment of iron, metals, etc.’

sampannaayalohādiupakaraṇo.meaning_2: possessing complete equipment of iron, metals, etc.; equipped with iron and metal wares
sampannaayalohādiupakaraṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound with sandhi; nominative singular masculine in the text, used in the phrase defining an aspiration for future material equipment. The form in the text is nominative singular.
sampannaayalohādiupakaraṇo.example_1: Iti me ayalohādayo siyuṃ anāgatamaddhānanti vā panettha nandiṃ samannāneti, imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā evaṃ sampannaayalohādiupakaraṇo bhavissāmī ’’ ti appaṭiladdhassa paṭilābhāya cittaṃ paṇidahati.
sampannaayalohādiupakaraṇo.translation_1: ‘May my iron and metals be like this in the future,’ or setting their mind on obtaining what they have not yet obtained by way of such methods as, ‘By this virtue or by this holy life, I will be one who possesses complete equipment of iron, metals, etc.’

ayalohādīnaṃ.meaning_2: iron and other metals; iron, copper, etc.
ayalohādīnaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is genitive plural (ayalohādīnaṃ), depending on sampattiṃ and vipattiṃ. The compound means 'iron, copper, and the like'.
ayalohādīnaṃ.example_1: Tathā attano ayalohādīnaṃ sampattiṃ vā vipattiṃ vā nissāya mānaṃ janeti ‘‘ imināhaṃ seyyosmīti vā, sadisosmīti vā hīnosmīti vā ’’ ti (vibha.832) evaṃ bāhiraṃ pathaviṃ mānamaññanāya maññati.
ayalohādīnaṃ.translation_1: Likewise, relying on the excellence or the failing of their own iron, metals, etc., they generate conceit: ‘I am superior’, ‘I am equal’, or ‘I am inferior’. Thus, they conceive external earth through conceit-conceiving.

khurakavātā.meaning_2: razor-like wind; wind sharp as a razor
khurakavātā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative plural (khurakavātā) in a list of internal winds. Same as satthakavāta and uppalakavāta.
khurakavātā.example_1: Vāyaṃ vāyatoti imassa vāyavārassāpi yojanānaye pana ‘‘ uddhaṅgamā vātā adhogamā vātā kucchisayā vātā koṭṭhāsayā vātā aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā satthakavātā khurakavātā uppalakavātā assāso passāso ’’ ti evaṃ vuttā ajjhattikā vāyodhātu.
khurakavātā.translation_1: In the Air Section, in the phrase “He perceives air as air,” in the method of explanation, the internal air element is what is spoken of: “up-going winds, down-going winds, winds in the belly, winds in the bowels, winds that course through the limbs, dagger-like winds, razor-like winds, lotus-like winds, in-breath and out-breath.”

asaṅkheyepi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (asaṅkheyye pi kappe: even in an incalculable aeon). Sandhi with -pi. The -eyya ending is from √khā (saṃ + √khā) with the ya sign.
asaṅkheyepi.example_1: Buddhā pana asaṅkheyepi kappe na uppajjanti, tadā suññāpi sā bhūmi hoti.
asaṅkheyepi.translation_1: For the Buddhas do not arise even in an incalculable aeon; in those times when a Buddha does not arise, that plane is empty.

tabbhūmikā.meaning_2: belonging to that plane; of that level; pertaining to that sphere
tabbhūmikā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it qualifies khandhā (masc nom pl). The PEU splits it as tabbhūmi + iya with the ya-ka suffix; iya and ika are alternative suffix forms of the same formation.
tabbhūmikā.translation_1: In that regard, the “dimension of infinite space” refers to the four aggregates of merit, fruit, and functional states belonging to that plane.

anibbānaṃyeva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of anibbānaṃ (nominative singular of anibbāna) and the emphatic particle yeva, with the initial y doubled after the niggahīta. Here it predicates the object grasped by the wrong view.
anibbānaṃyeva.example_1: Anibbānaṃyeva samānaṃ taṃ nibbānato niccādito ca gaṇhanto diṭṭhimaññanāya maññatīti veditabbo.
anibbānaṃyeva.translation_1: While it is not Nibbana, one who grasps it as Nibbana, as permanent, and so on, conceives through the conceit of views; this should be understood.

bāḷhaso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverb formed from bāḷha (strong, intense) with the suffix -so. In the sentence it modifies haññati: 'is constantly struck forcefully'. Not bāḷha + sati as the PEU suggests.
bāḷhaso.example_1: Rogādīhi ca dukkhehi, niccaṃ haññati bāḷhaso.
bāḷhaso.translation_1: And by pains and sickness, is constantly struck with force.

pariggāhalakkhaṇaṃ.meaning_2: having the characteristic of possession; with grasping as its characteristic
pariggāhalakkhaṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter in the text (nominative singular) as the predicate of sammāvācāya; the compound may also be taken as a neuter noun 'characteristic of grasping'. Printed as a compound resolving to sammāvācāya pariggāhalakkhaṇaṃ; the form is a compound, not sandhi, so root fields are empty.
pariggāhalakkhaṇaṃ.translation_1: The characteristic of taking up of right speech.

aviciṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text; name of the lowest hell, paired with bhavagga as the lower limit.
aviciṃ.example_1: Upari bhavaggaṃ heṭṭhā aviciṃ pariyantaṃ katvā tiriyaṃ aparimāṇāsu lokadhātūsu sabbasatte abhibhavati, sīlenapi samādhināpi paññāyapi vimuttiyāpi vimuttiñāṇadassanenapi, na tassa tulā vā pamāṇaṃ vā atthi, atulo appameyyo anuttaro rājarājo devadevo sakkānaṃ atisakko brahmānaṃ atibrahmā.
aviciṃ.translation_1: Having taken the highest heaven as the limit above and the Avīci hell as the limit below, he overcomes all beings in immeasurable world-systems through virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation. He has no equal or measure; he is incomparable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, king of kings, god of gods, supreme over Sakka, and supreme over Brahmā.

adiṭṭhamatulitamatīritamasacchikataṃ.meaning_2: not seen, not weighed or compared, not investigated, not realised
adiṭṭhamatulitamatīritamasacchikataṃ.construction: a + diṭṭha + a + tulita + a + matīrita + a + sacchikata
adiṭṭhamatulitamatīritamasacchikataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of adiṭṭha + atulita + amatīrita + asacchikata; in the text the series is adiṭṭha, atulita, amatīrita, asacchikata, all negated by a- and compounded with -a- joining. Nominative singular neuter, agreeing with saṅkhāragataṃ.
adiṭṭhamatulitamatīritamasacchikataṃ.example_1: Buddhānaṃ pana aṇuppamāṇampi saṅkhāragataṃ ñāṇena adiṭṭhamatulitamatīritamasacchikataṃ natthi.
adiṭṭhamatulitamatīritamasacchikataṃ.translation_1: But for the Buddhas, there is no state of formation, not even the smallest amount, that has not been seen, weighed, investigated, and realized by their knowledge.

tihāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A sandhi of ti + ha + iti, quoted in the commentary; possibly to be read as the emphatic particles ti and ha with iti.

yidha.meaning_2: here; in this case; on this point
yidha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ (or idaṃ) with idha, in the phrase na yidha puna vattabbam atthi ('there is nothing further to be said here'). Could also be analysed as idha with prothetic y-, or as yaṃ + idha; the text's sandhi form is kept as headword.
yidha.example_1: Vuttamidaṃ imassa suttassa nikkhepavicāraṇāyaṃ eva ‘‘ mānabhañjanatthaṃ sabbadhammamūlapariyāyanti desanaṃ ārabhī ’’ ti, tasmā na yidha puna vattabbamatthi, evaṃ mānabhañjanatthaṃ desitañca panetaṃ suttaṃ sutvā te bhikkhū taṃyeva kira pathaviṃ diṭṭhigatikopi sañjānāti, sekkhopi arahāpi tathāgatopi sañjānāti.
yidha.translation_1: It is said in the inquiry into the opening of this sutta: ‘He began the teaching of the Mūlapariyāya Sutra in order to break their pride’, therefore there is nothing more to be said here; and having heard this teaching given to break their pride, those bhikkhus thought, ‘Indeed, even a person with wrong views knows this same earth, as do those in training, Arahants, and the Tathāgata’.

sanighaṇṭukeṭubhānaṃ.meaning_2: together with the Nighaṇṭu and Keṭubha texts; with the glossary and the ritual manual
sanighaṇṭukeṭubhānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural in the text, qualifying vedānaṃ. The two texts are Brahmanical ancillary works on synonyms and on ritual.
sanighaṇṭukeṭubhānaṃ.example_1: Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, aññataro disāpāmokkho brāhmaṇo bārāṇasiyaṃ paṭivasati tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇṭukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ padako veyyākaraṇo lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo, so pañcamattāni māṇavakasatāni mante vāceti.
sanighaṇṭukeṭubhānaṃ.translation_1: ‘Formerly, bhikkhus, a certain world-famed Brahmin lived in Benares, a master of the three Vedas, along with the Nighaṇṭu and Keṭubha texts, phonology and etymology, and the histories as a fifth, a grammarian, fully versed in natural philosophy and in the marks of a great man; he taught hymns to five hundred young brahmin students.’

bhūtapacaniṃ.meaning_2: craving that cooks beings; that which roasts beings
bhūtapacaniṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (bhūtapacaniṃ). Com commentarial gloss: taṇhā which cooks (pacati) beings in the states of loss. The compound is built from bhūta + paca with the agent suffix -yu and ī.
bhūtapacaniṃ.example_1: Yo ca kālaghaso bhūto, sa bhūtapacaniṃ pacī ’’ ti.(jā.1.10.190)–
bhūtapacaniṃ.translation_1: “But that being who has consumed time, has cooked the cooker of beings.”
bhūtapacaniṃ.example_2: Sa bhūtapacaniṃ pacīti so yāyaṃ taṇhā apāyesu bhūte pacati, taṃ ñāṇagginā paci dayhi bhasmamakāsi, tena ‘‘ bhūtapacaniṃ pacī ’’ ti vuccati.
bhūtapacaniṃ.translation_2: ‘“Has cooked the cooker of beings” means that craving which cooks beings in the states of loss—he has cooked, i.e., burned, that craving with the fire of path-knowledge, making it like ash, therefore he is called “cooker of beings”.’

dayhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text dayhi is the aorist 3rd singular (or a truncated aorist), glossed bhasmamakāsi 'made into ash'; the PEU also gives dayhi = daha + ya + ā 'is burned', from dayhati.
dayhi.example_1: Sa bhūtapacaniṃ pacīti so yāyaṃ taṇhā apāyesu bhūte pacati, taṃ ñāṇagginā paci dayhi bhasmamakāsi, tena ‘‘ bhūtapacaniṃ pacī ’’ ti vuccati.
dayhi.translation_1: ‘“Has cooked the cooker of beings” means that craving which cooks beings in the states of loss—he has cooked, i.e., burned, that craving with the fire of path-knowledge, making it like ash, therefore he is called “cooker of beings”.’

pajanintipi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form is pajāninti + pi, 3rd plural present with emphatic -pi; root √ñā becomes jānā with the -nā sign and the pa prefix.

kākandī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text, part of a list of city names illustrating how grammarians explain names. Nominative singular. The commentarial tradition connects it with the hermit Kākanda.
kākandī.example_1: Tatrāyaṃ apubbapadavaṇṇanā – sāvatthīti savatthassa isino nivāsaṭṭhānabhūtā nagarī, yathā kākandī mākandī kosambīti evaṃ tāva akkharacintakā.
kākandī.translation_1: Here is the explanation of the preceding terms: “Sāvatthī” is the city that was the residence of the seer Savattha, as in the cases of Kākandī, Mākandī, and Kosambī; this is how the grammarians first interpret it.

mākandī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a city mentioned alongside Kākandī and Kosambī in the commentary, illustrating how the grammarians explain place names. Nominative singular in the text. Feminine form of mākanda.
mākandī.example_1: Tatrāyaṃ apubbapadavaṇṇanā – sāvatthīti savatthassa isino nivāsaṭṭhānabhūtā nagarī, yathā kākandī mākandī kosambīti evaṃ tāva akkharacintakā.
mākandī.translation_1: Here is the explanation of the preceding terms: “Sāvatthī” is the city that was the residence of the seer Savattha, as in the cases of Kākandī, Mākandī, and Kosambī; this is how the grammarians first interpret it.

saṃvaraṃbraūmi.meaning_2: I speak of restraint; I declare restraint
saṃvaraṃbraūmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of saṃvaraṃ (accusative of saṃvara) and braūmi (1st singular present of brūti). Quoted from Sn 1041.
saṃvaraṃbraūmi.example_1: Tathā hi ‘‘ anujānāmi, bhikkhave, divā paṭisallīyantena dvāraṃ saṃvaritvā paṭisallīyitun ’’ ti (pārā.77),‘‘ sotānaṃ saṃvaraṃbraūmi, paññāyete pidhīyare ’’ ti (su. ni.1041) ca ādīsu pidhānaṭṭhena saṃvaramāha.
saṃvaraṃbraūmi.translation_1: Indeed, it speaks of restraint in the sense of covering in such places as “Monks, I allow one who is resting in the daytime to rest having restrained the door,” and “I speak of the restraint of streams; they are closed off by wisdom.”

saccappaṭikulena.meaning_2: averse to the truth; contrary to the truth
saccappaṭikulena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text instrumental singular, modifying cittassa; part of a definition of ayoniso manasikāra. Probably a compound with paṭikula (disagreeable; averse), though which of the two component words is meant (sacca + paṭikula or a form of paṭikūla) is uncertain.
saccappaṭikulena.example_1: Saccappaṭikulena vā cittassa āvaṭṭanā anvāvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro, ayaṃ vuccati ayoniso manasikāroti.
saccappaṭikulena.translation_1: Or, it is the turning, the successive turning, the engagement, the focusing, and the mental settling of the mind in a manner contrary to the truths.

pahātabbātiādimāha.meaning_2: he said starting with 'to be abandoned'
pahātabbātiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of a potential participle, the quotative iti, ādi and the aorist āha. The word is a commentarial phrase; the main word is pahātabbā.

yenā.meaning_2: by which; by whom; through which; by which means; where
yenā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these sentences yena is the instrumental of the relative pronoun ya, often with the locative sense (bhummatthe karaṇavacanaṃ). The final -a is lengthened before the quotation ti.
yenā.example_1: Yenā ākārena manasikariyamānā akusaluppattipadaṭṭhānā honti, tenākārena na manasikātabbā.
yenā.translation_1: One should not attend to things in such a way that they become the footing for the arising of unwholesome states.
yenā.example_2: Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamīti yenāti bhummatthe karaṇavacanaṃ, tasmā yattha bhagavā, tattha upasaṅkamīti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo.
yenā.translation_2: Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamī: herein, yena is an instrumental case used in the sense of a locative; therefore, the meaning should be understood as: 'where the Blessed One was, to that place he approached'.

kāmāsavotiādimāha.meaning_2: “kāmāsavo” (the influx of sensual desire) — thus, starting from that, he said; “kāmāsavo” etc. he said
kāmāsavotiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kāmāsavo, iti, ādiṃ (or ādimāha = ādiṃ + āha) and āha. Quotation followed by iti; āha is the perfect of √brū. No sentence given, so the exact segmentation is uncertain.

diṭṭhīnantiādimāha.meaning_2: ‘with views’ — that is what he said; ‘diṭṭhīnaṃ’ … so he began (the exposition); he said this beginning with (the words) ‘of views’
diṭṭhīnantiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentarial sandhi resolving to diṭṭhīnaṃ (genitive plural of diṭṭhi) + ti + ādim + āha (aorist of brūti, ‘he said’); a stock commentarial phrase introducing a quotation. The first element is printed with a single -ī- (diṭṭhīna-), a common commentarial spelling for diṭṭhīnaṃ.

vavatthāpayato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative present participle vavatthāpayato (genitive/dative singular) in the text; the main clause has the finite form vavatthapeti.
vavatthāpayato.example_1: Taṃ vavatthāpayato uppanne tadārammaṇe cittacetasike dhamme ime cattāro arūpakkhandhāti vavatthapeti.
vavatthāpayato.translation_1: To one defining that, the arising of the mental and physical states having that as an object defines these four as 'the mental aggregates.'

yañhissātiādimhi.meaning_2: in the passage beginning 'yaṃ hi ssāti'; in the phrase beginning 'yaṃ hissāti'
yañhissātiādimhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quotation joined by sandhi, referring to a passage beginning yaṃ hi ssāti; locative singular of ādimhi. Alternative analysis: yaṃ + hissāti + ādimhi.

yekārassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text (yekārassa). Grammatical term in the commentary, referring to the letter 'ya' in 'ye-kārassa yan ti ādeso'. Sometimes written as two words ye-kārassa.
yekārassa.translation_1: Or else, the letter ‘ya’ is a substitute for ‘yaṃ’.

yañhissāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ and hissati (fut of √hi, 'will send'), quoted with ti. No sentence available for confirmation.

līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhanakāmasukhattak.meaning_2: sluggishness, restlessness, contraction, grasping, indulgence in sensual pleasure, indulgence in self-mortification, annihilationism and eternalism and so on
līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhanakāmasukhattak.construction: līna + uddhacca + patiṭṭhāna + āyūhana + kāmasukhattakilamatha + anuyoga + uccheda + sassata + abhinivesa + ādi
līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhanakāmasukhattak.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A long compound of disturbances (upaddava) countered by the factors of awakening. Genitive plural in the text (…ādīnaṃ). The compound may be grouped as līna, uddhacca, patiṭṭhāna, āyūhana, kāmasukhattakilamathānuyoga, ucchedasassatābhinivesa, ādi; the text splits it as kāmasukhattakilamathānuyoga-ucchedasassatābhinivesa.
līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhanakāmasukhattak.example_1: Yā hi ayaṃ dhammasāmaggī, yāya lokiyalokuttaramaggakkhaṇe uppajjamānāya līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhana-kāmasukhattakilamathānuyoga-ucchedasassatābhinivesādīnaṃ anekesaṃ upaddavānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtāya satidhammavicayavīriyapītipassaddhisamādhiupekkhāsaṅkhātāya dhammasāmaggiyā ariyasāvako bujjhatīti katvā ‘‘ bodhī ’’ ti vuccati.
līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhanakāmasukhattak.translation_1: This is a synthesis of states because, through this synthesis of states—which consists of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, concentration, and equanimity, and which serves as the counter-agent to many disturbances such as sluggishness, restlessness, contraction, grasping, the indulgence in sensual pleasure, the indulgence in self-mortification, and the annihilationist and eternalist views that arise during the mundane and supra-mundane moments of the path—an noble disciple awakens; and so it is called ‘enlightenment’.

līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhana.meaning_2: sluggishness, restlessness, the fixing (of the mind), and striving; indolence and agitation with settling and exertion
līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhana.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A four-member dvandva in the commentary's list of the hindrances and their related states; part of a longer compound in the text. The exact division is uncertain: possibly līna + uddhacca + patiṭṭhāna + āyūhana, or patiṭṭhāna + āyūhana may belong with the following kāmasukhattakilamathānuyoga. The meaning 'fixing of the mind' for patiṭṭhāna is from context.
līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhana.example_1: Yā hi ayaṃ dhammasāmaggī, yāya lokiyalokuttaramaggakkhaṇe uppajjamānāya līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhana-kāmasukhattakilamathānuyoga-ucchedasassatābhinivesādīnaṃ anekesaṃ upaddavānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtāya satidhammavicayavīriyapītipassaddhisamādhiupekkhāsaṅkhātāya dhammasāmaggiyā ariyasāvako bujjhatīti katvā ‘‘ bodhī ’’ ti vuccati.
līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhana.translation_1: This is a synthesis of states because, through this synthesis of states—which consists of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, concentration, and equanimity, and which serves as the counter-agent to many disturbances such as sluggishness, restlessness, contraction, grasping, the indulgence in sensual pleasure, the indulgence in self-mortification, and the annihilationist and eternalist views that arise during the mundane and supra-mundane moments of the path—an noble disciple awakens; and so it is called ‘enlightenment’.

tokāro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used in commentary to refer to the particle 'to' in the phrase 'yato kho'; nominative singular in the text.
tokāro.example_1: Tattha yato khoti sāmivacane tokāro, yassa khoti vuttaṃ hoti.
tokāro.translation_1: In the phrase ‘when indeed’, the particle ‘to’ is in the possessive case; it means ‘of whom’.

saṃchindi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular active of saṃchindati, used in the commentary to gloss acchecchi with chindi, saṃchindi, samucchindi, a series of near-synonyms for 'cut off'.
saṃchindi.example_1: Acchecchi taṇhanti sabbampi taṇhaṃ chindi, saṃchindi samucchindi.
saṃchindi.translation_1: ‘Has cut off craving’ means has cut, completely cut, utterly cut off all craving.

āḷulite.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally with bhattapakkhepena, meaning 'stirred up by the throwing of food'. Locative singular in the text.
āḷulite.example_1: Parittodake eva hi bhattapakkhepena āḷulite sukhumapāṇakā maranti, na mahātaḷākādīsūti.
āḷulite.translation_1: In reality, if one throws food into shallow water, the tiny beings die due to the disturbance; but they do not die in large ponds and the like.

sotiādimāha.meaning_2: so at the beginning (of the sentence) he said; thus beginning he said
sotiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of so, ti, ādi and āha (perfect of brūti, 'he said'). Conjectural analysis; no sentence context was available.

hetūtiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of hetū ('causes', nom/voc pl.) + iti + ādi ('beginning') + āha ('he said'). Explanation of the lemma's abbreviated citation form, as found in commentarial style; the last word āha is an irregular aorist of √ah (say).

asaṃlekhassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text. Though the input form has a double s, the lemma is asaṃlekha.
asaṃlekhassa.example_1: Esa nayo asantuṭṭhiyā asaṃlekhassa cuppannassa nivāraṇe.
asaṃlekhassa.translation_1: This is the same method for restraining discontent and lack of expunging that has arisen.

saṃlekhāya.meaning_2: effacement; expunging; wearing away (of defilements); austerity
saṃlekhāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative singular in the text (saṃvattissati takes the dative). Commentary gloss for effacing defilements; sometimes spelled sallekha.
saṃlekhāya.example_1: Evaṃ tāvassa appicchatāya santuṭṭhiyā saṃlekhāya saṃvattissati.
saṃlekhāya.translation_1: Thus it will lead him to modesty, contentment, and expunging.

khotiādimāhaṃsu.meaning_2: they said starting with 'kho ti'; they began to say 'kho'
khotiādimāhaṃsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kho ti ādi and āhaṃsu (aorist of āha). An alternative analysis is kho + ti-ādi + amhāsu. Commentary phrase introducing a quotation.

avagamanaṭṭhena.meaning_2: in the sense of going down; with the meaning of descending
avagamanaṭṭhena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text (avagamanaṭṭhena). avagamana = ava + gamana, 'going down, descending'; aṭṭha here = 'sense, meaning'.
avagamanaṭṭhena.example_1: Okkamane pubbaṅgamāti ettha okkamanaṃ vuccanti avagamanaṭṭhena pañca nīvaraṇāni, tena pañcanīvaraṇapubbaṅgamāti vuttaṃ hoti.
avagamanaṭṭhena.translation_1: Regarding okkamane pubbaṅgamā: here, the five hindrances are called okkamana in the sense of 'downward-going' (leading to lower realms), and by that it is meant that they are the precursors in fulfilling the five hindrances.

aripahānāya.meaning_2: abandonment of enemies; removal of the enemy
aripahānāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative singular in the text: 'for the abandonment of enemies'. Part of a threefold explanation of 'ariya' in the commentary.
aripahānāya.example_1: Aripahānāya saṃvattatītipi ariyena desitotipi ariyabhāvappaṭilābhāya saṃvattatītipi ariyo.
aripahānāya.translation_1: It is noble because it leads to the abandonment of enemies, because it is taught by the Noble One, and because it leads to the acquisition of the noble state.

madaggāhaṇaraso.meaning_2: having the function of grasping intoxication; whose flavour is the seizing of intoxication
madaggāhaṇaraso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing mada. Nominative singular in -o in the text (mado ... madaggāhaṇaraso).
madaggāhaṇaraso.translation_1: Intoxication has the characteristic of being intoxicated; it has the function of being seized by intoxication, and manifests as madness.

nivedetuṃ.meaning_2: to declare; to announce; to make known; to inform
nivedetuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of nivedeti (causative of ni + √vid). In the text it depends on āgato: 'came ... to declare'. The PEU gloss 'let me know' is not an infinitive sense here.
nivedetuṃ.example_1: So taṃ pasādaṃ nivedetuṃ bhagavato santikaṃ āgato, tasmā evamāha.
nivedetuṃ.translation_1: He came into the Blessed One's presence to declare that confidence, and therefore he spoke thus.

veditabbānī.meaning_2: to be understood; to be known
veditabbānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle, neuter nominative plural in the text, agreeing with vanapatthāni and padāni. From vijānāti; often glossed jānitabba.
veditabbānī.example_1: Ettha ca pariyantānanti imamekaṃ pariyāyaṃ ṭhapetvā sesapariyāyehi vanapatthāni veditabbānī.
veditabbānī.translation_1: And herein, setting aside this one interpretation of pariyantānan, the others are to be understood as forest-wildernesses through the remaining interpretations.
veditabbānī.example_2: Eteneva nayena avasesapadānipi atthato veditabbānī ’’ ti.
veditabbānī.translation_2: By this same method, the remaining phrases should be understood according to their meaning.”

ārammaṇapariggāhayuttānaṃ.meaning_2: engaged in grasping objects; occupied with taking up sense objects
ārammaṇapariggāhayuttānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural in the text. Part of a contrast: dwellings are hard to obtain for those lacking ārammaṇapariggāha, not for those engaged in it. The compound likely means 'associated with grasping at the objects of meditation'. Could also be taken as 'connected with the acquisition of a basis'.
ārammaṇapariggāhayuttānaṃ.example_1: 35. Athassa bhagavā purimanayeneva ‘‘ evametaṃ brāhmaṇā ’’ tiādīhi taṃ taṃ vacanaṃ sampaṭicchitvā abbhanumoditvā ca yasmā soḷasasu ṭhānesu ārammaṇapariggaharahitānaṃyeva tādisāni senāsanāni durabhisambhavāni, na tesu ārammaṇapariggāhayuttānaṃ, attanā ca bodhisatto samāno tādiso ahosi, tasmā attano tādisānaṃ senāsanānaṃ durabhisambhavataṃ dassetuṃ, mayhampi khotiādimāha.
ārammaṇapariggāhayuttānaṃ.translation_1: 35. Then, the Blessed One, having accepted and rejoiced in those respective statements according to the earlier method, beginning with, “That is so, brahmin,” wishing to show that such dwellings are difficult to endure because they are hard for those lacking the grasping of objects in these sixteen instances—though not for those engaged in grasping objects in them—and because he himself, while a Bodhisatta, was like that, he spoke the words starting with, “To me too, brahmin.”

lālamukhāti.meaning_2: with a drooling mouth; with a slobbering mouth; with a slimy mouth
lālamukhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The word in the text is lālamukhāti, which is lālamukhā + iti; the entry is for the compound adjective lālamukha. In the commentary it explains a term for someone with a slimy or drooling mouth. The nominative plural lālamukhā is used in the text.
lālamukhāti.translation_1: It is said that they have drooling mouths.

elamugāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of elamukāti? Probably elamuga + iti, a vocative addressed to Elamuga. No sentences supplied.

mayhantiādimāha.meaning_2: ‘do not kill’ — thus he said at the beginning; he said ‘mā hanti’ at first
mayhantiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mā, hanti, ādiṃ and āha; the commentary word introducing a quoted phrase. Alternative segmentation mā + hanti + ādim + āha with hanti as 3rd singular of hanati. No sentence context supplied.

lakkhaṇīyā.meaning_2: to be marked; to be designated; to be noted; to be characterised
lakkhaṇīyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used in the commentary to gloss abhilakkhitā; nominative singular feminine agreeing with the feminine subject, though the form is the same as the masculine stem and the neuter nominative.
lakkhaṇīyā.example_1: Abhilakkhitāti ettha upasaggamattameva, tasmā abhilakkhitāti lakkhaṇīyā icceva attho, uposathasamādānadhammassavanapūjāsakkārādikaraṇatthaṃ lakkhetabbā sallakkhetabbā upalakkhetabbāti vuttaṃ hoti.
lakkhaṇīyā.translation_1: In the phrase “abhilakkhitā,” it is merely an intensifier; therefore, ‘abhilakkhitā’ simply means ‘designated’ (lakkhaṇīyā). It is said to mean ‘to be noted’ or ‘to be marked’ for the purpose of carrying out duties such as observing the Uposatha, listening to the Dhamma, or making offerings.

bhavito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed in the commentary with bhūto santo vattamāno, describing one who is or remains in a posture. Nominative singular in the text.
bhavito.example_1: Tathābhūtaṃ tathābhūto vāti tena teneva iriyāpathena bhūto bhavito santo vattamāno samaṅgībhūto vāti attho.
bhavito.translation_1: “Tathābhūtaṃ tathābhūto vā” means, ‘Being, having been, or remaining in that very posture,’—this is the meaning.

parivicinanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle modifying the Bodhisatta, nominative singular masculine, alongside parivīmaṃsanto. Probably from parivicināti (vi + √ci with -nā-).
parivicinanto.example_1: So kho ahaṃ … pe … paṭivinemīti bodhisattassa kira caṅkamantassa tasmiṃ magasiṅgakhurasaddādibhede bhayabheravārammaṇe āgate neva mahāsatto tiṭṭhati, na nisīdati na sayati, atha kho caṅkamantova parivīmaṃsanto parivicinanto bhayabheravaṃ na passati, magasiṅgakhurasaddādimattameva cetaṃ hoti, so taṃ ñatvā idaṃ nāmetaṃ, na bhayabheravanti tato tiṭṭhati vā nisīdati vā sayati vā.
parivicinanto.translation_1: “So kho ahaṃ … paṭivinemī” means: It is said that when the Bodhisatta was walking, if that fear-inducing object came—whether a deer or the sound of antlers or hooves—the Great Being would not stand, nor sit, nor lie down; rather, while still walking, he would inquire and examine until he no longer saw the fear and terror, recognizing that it was merely the sound of a deer’s antlers or hooves. Having known that, and thinking, ‘This is that, not fear or terror,’ only then would he stand, sit, or lie down.

ravanakasakuṇā.meaning_2: bird that cries out; calling bird; noisy bird
ravanakasakuṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of ravanaka (crying, calling) and sakuṇa (bird). In the commentary it refers to birds such as crows that cry at night and owls that cry during the day. Nominative plural in the text.
ravanakasakuṇā.example_1: Atha divā ravanakasakuṇā kākādayo candālokena divāti maññamānā rattiṃ ravanti, aññehi vā kāraṇehi.
ravanakasakuṇā.translation_1: During the day, birds that cry out, such as crows, cry out at night because they think it is day due to moonlight, or for other reasons.
ravanakasakuṇā.example_2: Atha rattiṃ ravanakasakuṇā ulūkādayo majjhanhikasamayepi tattha tattha samandhakāre nilīnā rattisaññāya vā aññehi vā kāraṇehi ravanti.
ravanakasakuṇā.translation_2: Then, birds that cry out at night, such as owls, cry out even at midday, hiding in darkness here and there, whether out of a perception of night or for other reasons.

diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikahitūpadesakoti.meaning_2: advisor of benefits for this life and the next
diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikahitūpadesakoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet of the Buddha in the commentary (through the perfection of wisdom). Nominative singular in the text, with -ti attached.
diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikahitūpadesakoti.translation_1: “Bahujanahitāyā” means for the benefit of the many; through the perfection of wisdom, he is an advisor of benefits for both this life and the next.

abhininnāmitamatteyeva.meaning_2: only when [the mind] has been directed; merely on being inclined
abhininnāmitamatteyeva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of abhininnāmitamatte (locative singular of abhininnāmitamatta, 'mere directing', from abhininnāmita + matta) and the emphatic particle eva. In the text it gives the sense 'just as soon as the mind is directed'. One syllable -e- is elided in the junction.
abhininnāmitamatteyeva.example_1: Te hi citte abhininnāmitamatteyeva anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranti, dibbena cakkhunā satte passanti.
abhininnāmitamatteyeva.translation_1: Indeed, they remember their manifold past lives as soon as they direct their minds, and they see beings with the divine eye.

tappaṭicchādakamohandhakāraviddhaṃsakade.meaning_2: by holding up the lamp of the teaching that destroys the darkness of delusion covering that
tappaṭicchādakamohandhakāraviddhaṃsakade.construction: taṃ + paṭicchādaka + moha + andhakāra + viddhaṃsaka + desanā + pajjota + dhāraṇa + ṇa
tappaṭicchādakamohandhakāraviddhaṃsakade.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Long compound with instrumental singular ending -ena. The final -ṇena represents the suffix -ṇ(a) (instrumental -ena); there is some doubt about the exact analysis of the last member, probably desanāpajjotadhāraṇa ('holding up the lamp of the teaching').
tappaṭicchādakamohandhakāraviddhaṃsakade.example_1: Evaṃ kassapassa bhagavato sāsanantaradhānato pabhuti micchādiṭṭhigahanapaṭicchannaṃ sāsanaṃ vivarantena, yathā mūḷhassa maggaṃ ācikkheyya, evaṃ kummaggamicchāmaggappaṭipannassa me saggamokkhamaggaṃ ācikkhantena, yathā andhakāre telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya, evaṃ mohandhakāre nimuggassa me buddhādiratanarūpāni apassato tappaṭicchādakamohandhakāraviddhaṃsakadesanāpajjotadhāraṇena mayhaṃ bhotā gotamena etehi pariyāyehi pakāsitattā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsitoti.
tappaṭicchādakamohandhakāraviddhaṃsakade.translation_1: So too, by opening the teaching which had been hidden by the thicket of false views since the disappearance of the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa; just as one would point out the way to one who is lost, so too, by pointing out the way to heaven and liberation to me who was following a wrong path, a false path; just as one would hold up a lamp in the darkness, so too, by holding up the lamp of the teaching that destroys the darkness of delusion which covers the jewels of the Buddha and the others, to me who was submerged in the darkness of delusion and not seeing the jewels of the Buddha and the others, Master Gotama has made the Dhamma clear in many ways through these methods.

esāhantiādimāha.meaning_2: this is the beginning; he said (starting with) 'esāhaṃ'
esāhantiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound quotation formula: esāhaṃ opens a passage, iti closes it, ādi means 'beginning', āha is 'he said'. The writer explains that the speaker began with esāhaṃ. Nothing certain is known about the exact segmentation; esā + ahaṃ is the most likely first part.

desabhāsākosallamiva.meaning_2: like skill in local languages; as if skilled in the dialects of the region
desabhāsākosallamiva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of desabhāsākosallaṃ (nominative singular) + iva. In the text it introduces a simile for sammutiparamatthakosallaṃ.
desabhāsākosallamiva.translation_1: Skill in conventional and ultimate discourse is like skill in local languages.

gahitabbā.meaning_2: to be taken; to be grasped; to be clung to
gahitabbā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle in the nominative singular masculine, agreeing with kilesā. Part of the phrase na gahitabbā: 'not to be clung to'.
gahitabbā.example_1: ‘‘ Ime kilesā nāma kakkhaḷā vāḷā jahitabbā na gahitabbā visaduṭṭhasallasadisā ’’ ti evaṃ yāthāvasarasatopi na jānāti.
gahitabbā.translation_1: One does not understand as they really are the facts that “these defilements are coarse, violent, should be abandoned, should not be clung to, and are like an arrow smeared with poison.”

lageyyuṃ.meaning_2: would stick (to); would cling (to); would hang (on)
lageyyuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person plural optative used in the sense of hanging (on a peg).
lageyyuṃ.example_1: Na ca naṃ rajāpatheti pubbe vuttappakāre ṭhāne anikkhipitvā karaṇḍamañjūsādīsu vā ṭhapeyyuṃ, paliveṭhetvā vā nāgadante lageyyuṃ.
lageyyuṃ.translation_1: And would not keep it in a dusty place means not leaving it in the place described before, but keeping it in a box or chest, or wrapping it up and hanging it on a peg.

nāvajjissati.meaning_2: will not attend to; will not reflect on
nāvajjissati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + āvajjissati (future 3rd singular of āvajjati). In the text: nāvajjissati taṃ nimittaṃ 'he will not attend to that sign'.
nāvajjissati.example_1: Catutthavāre subhanimittaṃ na manasi karissatīti tasmiṃ sativirahābhāvato taṃ nimittaṃ nāvajjissati, sesaṃ dutiyavārānusārena veditabbaṃ.
nāvajjissati.translation_1: In the fourth sequence, will not attend to the beautiful sign means because he has no lack of mindfulness regarding that, he will not reflect on that sign; the rest should be understood according to the second sequence.

uñchitvā.meaning_2: having gleaned; having gathered scraps; having begged (for food)
uñchitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of uñchati (√uñch, glean). In the commentary passage it describes collecting scraps of food in villages. The PEU entry's 'having sought' is too general; 'gleaned' is more precise.
uñchitvā.example_1: Evaṃ pākaṭo ca ayasābhibhūto gāmasatampi pavisitvā ummārasatesu ṭhānesu uñchitvā yathādhotena pattena nikkhamati.
uñchitvā.translation_1: And having become known in this way, he is overcome by disrepute; he enters a hundred villages, wipes his feet at a hundred thresholds, and departs with an empty bowl.

paṭisallo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Paired with paṭisattu (an enemy) in the commentary; nominative singular. Not related to paṭisallāna (seclusion), despite the similar form.
paṭisallo.example_1: Imehi āpattādīhi asadisattā paṭisattu paṭisallo codako bhavituṃ ayuttoti vuttaṃ hoti.
paṭisallo.translation_1: It is said that a rival or an opponent who is a accuser is unsuitable to be a accuser because he is not the same in terms of offenses and so on.

byātipi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form byātipi is byāti with the emphatic particle -pi. The PEU gloss 'he opens eyes' is uncertain; the word is not found in the supplied sentences.

asakkārakaraṇāditāti.meaning_2: the state of showing disrespect and so on; disrespect and similar behaviour
asakkārakaraṇāditāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Non-compound reading: a-sakkāra-karaṇa-ādi-tā. Nominative singular in the text, ending a quotation. The sandhi -tāti = tā + iti.
asakkārakaraṇāditāti.example_1: Tatrāyaṃ upamāsaṃsandanā – parisuddhakaṃsapātisadisaṃ imassa pabbajjāliṅgaṃ, kuṇaparacanaṃ viya icchāvacarānaṃ appahānaṃ, aparakaṃsapātiyā paṭikujjhanaṃ viya āraññikaṅgādīhi icchāvacarappaṭicchādanaṃ, kaṃsapātiṃ vivaritvā kuṇapadassanena janassa amanāpatā viya āraññikaṅgādīni anādiyitvā icchāvacaradassanena sabrahmacārīnaṃ asakkārakaraṇāditāti.
asakkārakaraṇāditāti.translation_1: In that context, this is the application of the simile: his outward form of renunciation is like the pure bronze bowl; the failure to abandon the spheres of wishes is like the preparation with the carcass; the covering up of the spheres of wishes by his practice of living in the forest and so on is like the covering with the other bronze bowl; and the lack of respect and so on shown by his fellow monks when they see his spheres of wishes without heeding his forest-dwelling is like the revulsion people feel upon opening the bronze bowl and seeing the carcass.

iṇabhayādīhi.meaning_2: debt and fear and so on; debt, danger and other such things
iṇabhayādīhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the commentary it glosses jīvikatthā: those oppressed by debt, fear and similar troubles. Ablative plural iṇabhayādīhi.
iṇabhayādīhi.example_1: Jīvikatthāti iṇabhayādīhi pīḷitā bahi jīvituṃ asakkontā idha jīvikatthikā hutvā.
iṇabhayādīhi.translation_1: ‘To earn a livelihood’ (jīvikatthā) means those who, being oppressed by fears of debt and the like and unable to live outside, have become seekers of livelihood here.

vedibbo.meaning_2: should be understood; should be known
vedibbo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here vedibbo is a typo or variant spelling of veditabbo, the potential participle of vetti. Nominative singular masculine, agreeing with attho. The comment is about the meaning of the phrase.
vedibbo.example_1: Tasmā sampannasīlāti paripuṇṇasīlā hutvātipi sīlasamaṅgino hutvātipi evamettha attho vedibbo.
vedibbo.translation_1: Therefore, in the phrase 'perfect in ethics', one should understand the meaning as being 'those whose ethics are complete' and 'those who are possessed of ethics'.

sampassitabbo.meaning_2: should be seen; should be observed; should be looked upon
sampassitabbo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive potential participle in the nominative singular, agreeing with piyacakkhu- (instrumental plural in the text: 'sampassitabbo' modifies the person to be looked upon).
sampassitabbo.example_1: Piyo ca assanti piyacakkhūhi sampassitabbo, sinehuppattiyā padaṭṭhānabhūto bhaveyyanti vuttaṃ hoti.
sampassitabbo.translation_1: 'May I be dear' means I should be looked upon with affectionate eyes, as a foundation for the arising of love.

idiso.meaning_2: like this; such; of this kind
idiso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of idaṃ + diso (from √dis 2). Nominative singular masculine agreeing with the subject in the text; used predictively: idiso ... piyo hoti.
idiso.example_1: Evaṃ bhagavā yasmā ‘‘ sabrahmacārīnaṃ piyo cassaṃ manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā ’’ ti ime cattāro dhamme ākaṅkhantena natthaññaṃ kiñci kātabbaṃ, aññadatthu sīlādiguṇasamannāgatena bhavitabbaṃ, idiso hi sabrahmacārīnaṃ piyo hoti manāpo garu bhāvanīyo.
idiso.translation_1: Thus, because the Blessed One said, 'If a mendicant should wish to be dear, pleasing, respected, and esteemed by spiritual companions, he need do nothing else, he should be possessed of the virtues of ethics,' such a person is dear, pleasing, respected, and esteemed by spiritual companions.

assantiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of assanti (from √as 1, 'they are') + ādiṃ + āha ('he said'); quotation form introducing a list, no sentence supplied so analysis is tentative.
